propositions: AGENTS.md currently states an unconditional preference for LSP symbol tools over grep, but this claim is false when symbols are referenced as string literals (e.g., monkeypatch.setattr) that the LSP cannot resolve.
LSP index can report stale line numbers after recent edits in the same session, whereas grep on the working tree provides current accuracy.
Grep produces false positives in comments and other non-semantic contexts that LSP does not, creating a trade-off between false negatives and false positives.
The current bare preference in AGENTS.md trains agents to discount the rule when it fails, creating a precondition risk for dependent stories A and B.
A decision table encoding the division of labour (semantic symbol resolution vs. string-literal patterns vs. working-tree line numbers) will make the rule safe for agents to follow literally.
